investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-01T12:35–12:36Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api's POST /api/agents call could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at the /v1/agents endpoint. Because the failure occurred at the very first network hop to the swarm gateway — before any agent was provisioned — no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, and all contract assertions remain unverifiable. This is an eval-detected infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency, not a confirmed user-traffic outage.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint) was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check calls POST /api/agents as its first step, which in turn proxies to the swarm gateway ELB. The gateway returned a 502 bad_gateway on all three attempts within a ~33-second window, preventing agent creation and causing complete evidence absence for all checks. The root cause is a connectivity or availability failure at the swarm gateway layer, not in the eval runner or its configuration. No suspect code changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to implicate a recent deployment.

[Possible] The swarm gateway service behind the ELB (the process handling /v1/agents) crashed or was restarting, causing the ELB to return 502 with no healthy backends.
